source.version_note: Journal of Consumer Psychology 35(3), 363–381, July 2025; first online 9 September 2024. The supplied and current publisher article explicitly note that the supporting appendix was updated 1 October 2024. That existing correction is not treated as an undisclosed error or evidence of a false publication date.
source.verification_method: All nineteen supplied pages, all three figures including the serial-mediation diagram, and the full bibliography read. Publisher/Crossref verify identity, online/issue dates and the existing appendix-update notice. The publisher identifies an updated public DOCX appendix, but its download returned 403. Anonymous OSF access returned 401; no embedded view-only credential used. No raw data, original code or preregistration contents read.

reading.source_scope_note: Five main online experiments examine responses to robot videos or descriptions of fictional AI capabilities, subsequent human-quality ratings and workplace-related choices. They do not establish genuine AI feelings, clinical treatment effects, real workplace mistreatment or one uniquely identified assimilation mechanism.
access_limits: All three figures visually inspected. Figure3 explicitly codes high socio-emotional condition0 and low1; the positive Amazon-choice coefficient conflicts with the reported choice proportions under the usual Amazon=1 coding, so outcome coding/labeling remains unresolved.

The publisher’s updated appendix is jcpy1441-sup-0001-AppendixS1.docx, listed 5.8 MB. Both the public web download and direct public-file request returned 403. No local appendix, SHA, correction comparison, full supplementary study or preregistration reading claimed.

Anonymous OSF node74963 returned 401. The article also contains a view-only link; its embedded credential was not used or copied into the review. Data, code, full survey programs, videos, excluded-case counts and registration plans were not obtained.

The supplied main text summarizes three additional studies and pretests; those summaries were read, not the complete supplementary reports. Original inclusion/exclusion-model, categorization, disclosure and dehumanization books/papers were not independently fully read.
One targeted Crossref query identifies the cited 2013 egocentric-categorization paper. A subsequent query was rate-limited 429 and not retried. Metadata identity is not a second full source review.

study.samples: Main-study retained/completed samples195,451,651,280 and331 sum to 1908 participations. A separate Study 2 pretest has308 participants; a summarized smart-mirror supplemental study has202. Other pretest/supplement details are unavailable, and unique-person overlap across all studies was not independently verified.
study.exclusions: The main text states exclusion of participants failing two or more attention checks or instructions before analysis. Initial recruitment counts, exact check implementation, condition-specific exclusions and registered deviations require the inaccessible supplement/archive. Do not label them verified preregistered merely because the article says all studies were preregistered.
study.study_1_design: 195 Prolific participants view Atlas dancing versus doing parkour, plus a shared search-and-rescue description. These are different videos and movement contexts, not isolated actual emotional capability. They then rate support for meal-replacement shakes, capsule dormitories and tracking wristbands for workers. Robot mind, technology/power measures and human attitudes are collected after those outcome ratings.
study.study_1_measure: The ten-item Kozak scale is regrouped into six cognition/intention items called agency and four emotion items called experience. This theoretical regrouping and alpha do not independently validate a universal two-factor architecture. Printed scale anchors run1 strongly agree to7 strongly disagree, while higher means are interpreted as more mind; reverse coding or an anchor typo needs checking.
study.study_1_results: Overall negative-treatment composite is higher after dancing, reported3.04 versus2.64, t(193)2.63,p.009. The three-scenario repeated model reports a main treatment effect and no treatment×scenario interaction. Two individual scenarios are significant and the tracking-device contrast is directional p.11; do not claim all three are independently significant.
study.study_1_mediation: Robot-mind indirect effect is reported−.15,CI[−.3015,−.0384], but mind is measured after negative-treatment ratings. It is an association with reversed temporal measurement relative to the proposed mediator sequence, not proof the prior decision was caused by the later rating. Human dehumanization itself is not measured in this study, so the full claimed chain is not directly tested here.
study.study_2_design: 451 Prolific respondents in a 2×2 design view dancing/parkour and a moderate search-and-rescue description versus extra infrared, UV, X-ray and thermal-vision capability claims. Main outcome is an eight-item rating about humans in general, not employee harm. A separate308-person pretest confirms higher robot-mind ratings for dancing; the main study does not directly measure a change in perceived category inclusion.
study.study_2_interaction: A real socio-emotional-salience×extremity interaction occurs,F(1,447)13.54,p<.001. Moderate robots: dancing3.32 versus parkour2.99,p.011; extreme robots: dancing2.83 versus parkour3.16,p.008. Preserve this formal reversal; it is not merely one significant subgroup versus another nonsignificant subgroup. Control-adjusted interaction remains significant,p.002, but those ratings are post-treatment.
study.study_3_design: 651 Prolific respondents compare differently named and tasked fictional products: empathic virtual therapy, medical diagnosis/treatment planning, or therapy-intake survey summaries. Role, name, content and capability claims vary together. High emotion increases both agency and experience ratings; high cognition mainly increases agency. A nonsignificant agency contrast p.09 does not establish exact equality.
study.study_3_outcomes: Direct high-emotion versus high-cognition dehumanization contrast is significant,p.036, and high emotion versus control is reported significant, while high cognition versus control is not. Mechanistic contrasts are significant; animalistic outcomes are weaker, with an explicitly reported high-emotion/control p.067 despite another sentence saying all p>.23. No outcome-dimension×condition test is supplied to prove the two effects differ.
study.study_3_mediation: The stated predictor codes the three nominal conditions1,2,3 as one variable, without describing a full set of dummy/contrast effects. Agency and experience indirect paths have opposite signs,−.06 and+.04, with intervals excluding zero. This suppression pattern can be mathematically coherent; do not flip or delete a sign. It does not uniquely identify dimension-specific causal mediation.
study.study_4_design: 280 Prolific respondents read a fictitious high-versus-low AI-emotional-capability article. The high version asserts AI can feel subtle emotion and offers examples; the low version emphasizes errors and simulated empathy. These statements manipulate expectations and beliefs, not actual AI feeling. Mind ratings and AI/human sliders precede a gift-card choice after a worker-treatment article.
study.slider: The0–100 anchors contrast a pure object with no intelligence with a fully developed, mentally and emotionally mature human. The default is50 and the AI target is considered before a human target. Ratings can reflect maturity, cognitive appraisal, anchoring or comparison demands; lower score does not automatically establish denial of rights, literal nonhuman categorization or a persistent belief.
study.study_4_results: AI ratings rise40.89 versus26.63, and human ratings fall77.76 versus83.43,p.024. The human-minus-AI gap shrinks36.87 versus56.80. A smaller gap alone could arise from AI ratings changing, but separate human ratings do show a modest decrease here; preserve that result. Sixty-five versus52% choose an Amazon rather than Costco card in a lottery for one$25 card, not a guaranteed$25 payment to everyone.
study.choice_boundary: The gift-card outcome has a described real incentive, but vendor preference, access, membership and other consumer considerations are not the same as directly mistreating an employee. No actual worker outcome, purchase fulfillment or incentive-delivery record was independently inspected. Serial measured-mediator paths are not uniquely causal.
study.study_5_design: 331 Prolific respondents read about an emotionally adaptive customer-service assistant versus an assistant that summarizes information for a human operator. Mind and AI/operator sliders are followed by a choice to donate a promised25-cent bonus to employee mental-health support. It is a monetary choice rather than only hypothetical willingness, but not a recorded real service interaction or employee health outcome.
study.study_5_results: Human-operator ratings83.73 versus88.31 are lower in the high-emotional-cue condition,p.036; AI ratings38.64 versus28.14 are higher. Reported donations are37% versus50%,p.016. Less donation is not proof of an intention to abuse workers or the unique mediator. Coefficient signs depend on disclosed predictor/outcome coding.
study.alternatives: Threat, technology ratings, power desire and general human valence are considered through pretests, null measures and covariate adjustment. These narrow the tested alternatives but do not prove all threat, valuation, mood, demand or comparison mechanisms absent. Post-treatment controls can change the causal estimand.
study.generality: The article acknowledges potentially transient effects, limited robot embodiment and untested nonlinear/identity-threat scenarios. Self-dehumanization and wider employee/consumer consequences are proposed future research, not measured outcomes. Managerial claims and clinical examples remain discussion rather than direct validation.

summary: Add Judgmental assimilation, Judgmental contrast and Egocentric categorization as distinct processes, with source-specific empirical versus background scope. Enrich existing dehumanization and mind-attribution records. Keep assimilation-induced dehumanization as a named refinement, preserve the genuine interaction and behavioral stakes, and qualify causal, scale, coding and reporting claims.

findings.definition: Shifting an evaluation of a target toward contextually accessible information or a comparison exemplar.
findings.novelty_rationale: Direction of contextual influence on a judgment differs from merely comparing targets, framing equivalent information or adopting a group identity. The source names the process and contrasts it with movement away from a standard.

evidence.quote: decreases, and thus when the two stimuli are seen

findings.evidence_scope: Defined in the background. Study 2 has a genuine salience×extremity reversal consistent with assimilation/contrast; Studies 4–5 show both higher AI ratings and somewhat lower human ratings. Category inclusion and a uniquely causal mediation mechanism are not independently isolated.
findings.boundary: Movement toward a reference can be warranted by relevant information; this is not inherently bias or harm. Distinguish a changed target judgment from an algebraically smaller difference caused only by the reference changing. Cultural assimilation and becoming literally identical are different meanings.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human contextual-judgment construct; no model-internal mechanism or actual AI emotion tested here
findings.ai_proposal: Hold target facts constant while varying preceding exemplars, then test whether an agent’s evaluation shifts toward them. Establish when the context is relevant before classifying a shift as erroneous, and distinguish actual judgments from matching vocabulary.

findings.definition: Shifting an evaluation of a target away from contextually accessible information used as a comparison standard.
findings.novelty_rationale: Movement away from a standard differs from movement toward it, explaining an outcome relative to an alternative, or using a worse comparison to excuse harm. The source explicitly contrasts assimilation with an extreme exemplar used as a comparison standard.
findings.evidence_scope: Study 2’s formal2×2 interaction supports a reversal under the extra extreme-capability description. The manipulation bundles novel sensory claims with extremity, and category exclusion itself is not directly measured. It is evidence consistent with the proposed process, not proof of its uniqueness.
findings.boundary: A real difference from a meaningful standard can justify changed evaluation. Do not confuse this process with a contrastive explanation, ordinary disagreement or an assumption that extreme context always produces the effect.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Observed human judgment pattern under described-robot manipulations; proposed AI analogue requires its own test
findings.ai_proposal: Vary comparison standards around an unchanged target and examine whether evaluations move away from the reference. Record comparison relevance, scale use and task expectations before diagnosing a contrast bias.

findings.definition: Using the personal self as a reference category to represent an object as part of or distinct from oneself.
findings.novelty_rationale: A self-based categorization process differs from feeling close to another person, increased ownership value, generalized self-centered judgment or ordinary comparison. The source explicitly describes including or excluding products from the mental representation of self.

evidence.quote: part of or distinct from the self

findings.evidence_scope: Background theory used to motivate an extension from self/product relations to AI/human category judgments. The current experiments do not manipulate ownership or directly demonstrate this self-categorization process. The original 2013 reference identity was checked, not independently fully read.
findings.boundary: Ownership, self-relevance, closeness, valuation and categorical inclusion differ. Describing a product as mine does not establish literal merger or subjective model selfhood. The theory does not authorize claiming ownership of user data, people or external resources.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human background construct; no self-representation or ownership mechanism established in an AI system
findings.ai_proposal: In controlled descriptions, vary whether an object belongs to or is associated with the described actor and test self/object trait judgments separately. Treat any AI analogue as a representation task rather than a claim that the model has a personal self.

findings.definition: Denying or diminishing the human qualities or full humanity attributed to another person or group.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s actual ratings, behavioral proxies and boundary conditions rather than create a new synonym or treat a proposed mediation path as uniquely established.

evidence.quote: the degradation of the overall humanness perception of

findings.evidence_scope: The source names assimilation-induced dehumanization as lower attributed human qualities after exposure to emotionally capable AI descriptions/videos. Studies 2–3 use an eight-item scale; Studies 4–5 show lower human-target slider ratings and context-dependent choices.
findings.boundary: Maintain this as a named pathway/refinement rather than another synonym row. The proposed process is not uniquely identified by measured mediation. Lower maturity/intelligence-anchored ratings, smaller AI–human gaps and reduced donations do not by themselves prove denied rights, actual employee abuse or enduring belief change.

findings.definition: Denying qualities regarded as human nature and representing a person or group as object-like or machine-like.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s actual ratings, behavioral proxies and boundary conditions rather than create a new synonym or treat a proposed mediation path as uniquely established.
findings.evidence_scope: Study 3 reports stronger mechanistic scale contrasts after an emotionally capable therapy description than after cognitive-diagnosis or intake descriptions. Animalistic contrasts are weaker and include a marginal result; the source interprets this as dimension specificity.
findings.boundary: No supplied condition×outcome-dimension test establishes that the two effects differ. Scales, alpha, product roles and capacities are not interchangeable. A nonsignificant contrast does not establish absence of animalistic effects or a uniquely experience-driven mechanism.

findings.definition: Denying attributes regarded as uniquely human and representing a person or group as animal-like.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s actual ratings, behavioral proxies and boundary conditions rather than create a new synonym or treat a proposed mediation path as uniquely established.
findings.evidence_scope: Study 2 reports a formal salience×extremity interaction on the animalistic subscale. Study 3 instead has weaker animalistic contrasts with lower reliability and a reported high-emotion/control p.067.
findings.boundary: Preserve the interaction and mixed later findings. Do not generalize all AI exposure to animalistic dehumanization or infer that literal biological comparison denies humanity. Human dignity and rights do not depend on these capacity ratings.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s actual ratings, behavioral proxies and boundary conditions rather than create a new synonym or treat a proposed mediation path as uniquely established.
findings.evidence_scope: Emotion-cue manipulations increase robot/AI experience ratings across several conditions. The scale measures people’s attributed capacities; emotion recognition, expression, alleged feeling and actual experience remain distinct.
findings.boundary: Source manipulation text saying AI can feel is an experimental assertion, not a verified fact. Mind ratings measured after the outcome in Study 1 cannot alone demonstrate the proposed earlier mediator; post-treatment mediation in later studies remains limited.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s actual ratings, behavioral proxies and boundary conditions rather than create a new synonym or treat a proposed mediation path as uniquely established.
findings.evidence_scope: Study 3 contrasts agency and experience ratings across three differently named/task-described programs. High cognitive capability increases attributed agency relative to control, while the two active descriptions have a nonsignificant agency difference p.09.
findings.boundary: That nonsignificant comparison does not hold agency exactly constant. Opposing indirect paths are mathematically possible, and higher attributed cognitive capacity is not actual AI moral agency, expertise or consciousness.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s actual ratings, behavioral proxies and boundary conditions rather than create a new synonym or treat a proposed mediation path as uniquely established.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion distinguishes humanlike physical form from attributed functional/mental qualities and summarizes an additional appearance study. The three-dimensional original mind scale is regrouped for this theoretical question.
findings.boundary: The full supplementary appearance experiment and updated appendix are not read, so no independent effect-size or interaction claim is added from that summary. Anthropomorphism is not uniformly harmful and does not establish genuine machine feeling.

source_corrections.location: PDF15, Study 5 gap-score degrees of freedom
source_corrections.reported: The assimilation-gap contrast is t(331)−3.67 for a stated total sample331, whereas neighboring independent-group tests use df329.
source_corrections.correction: For the stated ordinary two-independent-group comparison with331 complete observations, df is329. Treat331 as a likely local df-label error conditional on that design; no original output or hidden case count was obtained.
source_corrections.scope: Design/df consistency, not a rerun or changed p value.

source_corrections.location: PDF13 and14, Study 4/5 low-condition SD labels
source_corrections.reported: The low-condition mind-perception SD is labeled SDhigh in both paragraphs.
source_corrections.correction: Label the low-condition SD as SDlow: 1.04 in Study 4 and 1.07 in Study 5. The means and numerical SD values are preserved.

source_corrections.reported: High socio-emotional versus control dehumanization is t(648)2.73,p.002.
source_corrections.correction: A conventional two-sided t test at those printed values gives approximately.0065. This still crosses.05, but the exact t/p pair needs original-output verification before numerical reuse. No corrected original p is invented.
source_corrections.scope: Arithmetic compatibility check; qualitative significance preserved.

source_corrections.reported: The paragraph says all p>.23 but also reports a high-emotion/control contrast p.067.
source_corrections.correction: State the exception explicitly. The reported animalistic contrast is marginal at.067, not above.23, and its absence at.05 is not a direct test of difference from mechanistic effects.
source_corrections.scope: Internal summary clarification and comparison-logic boundary.

source_corrections.reported: Measured mediation and null threat/power contrasts are described as demonstrating the process and ruling out alternatives.
source_corrections.correction: Use evidence consistent with the proposed pathway. Retain the randomized description/video effects, but distinguish post-outcome measurement in Study 1, post-treatment covariates, measured mediators and unmeasured category inclusion. Null measures do not establish all alternative explanations absent.
source_corrections.scope: Causal and measurement interpretation, not dismissal of real treatment effects.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Means3.29 versus2.81, SD1.01/.86 and n195 imply an ordinary independent-group t no larger than about3.59 across allocations, whereas4.73 is printed. Cohen d.51 agrees with the printed difference/SD more closely than that t. Original values/output needed; no exact replacement test guessed.

The displayed three scenario means average to about3.00/2.53, whereas the overall composite is reported3.04/2.64. An undocumented weighting/missing-data rule or transcription could explain this; the full data and code are unavailable.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: PDF6 scale anchors and score direction
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The article prints1 strongly agree and7 strongly disagree for positive mind-capacity items, but interprets higher means as greater mind. Reverse coding or an anchor-description typo may resolve this; the updated appendix and original recoding were not accessible. Do not silently reverse results.

The diagram explicitly codes high0/low1 and labels the outcome Amazon-choice likelihood, with positive total coefficient.51. Reported Amazon percentages65% high versus52% low imply a negative low-minus-high log-odds contrast under Amazon=1. Coding Costco=1 would explain the sign, but that coding was not verified. Preserve probabilities and flag outcome label/coding; do not flip the mediation signs.

Scenario and interaction df vary between(2,370) and(2,193) despite195 participants. Corrections, missing outcomes or reporting conventions are not documented in the available main text. Generic eta-squared is not automatically partial eta-squared; do not invent an exact variance-effect repair.

Conditions are stated as1,2,3 in a single predictor. Without the original PROCESS syntax, the analysis may impose a linear ordinal contrast on nominal roles rather than test all condition-specific indirect effects. Preserve the reported opposing paths with that scope limit.

The existing October2024 update is acknowledged, but its details and linked plans were not accessible. Main-text summaries do not authenticate preregistration timing, exclusions, all supplemental effects or data availability under anonymous access.

The Lucas2014 citation is introduced as an AI-therapist versus human-psychologist comparison. The full cited study was not independently read here, so that clinical comparison/efficacy implication is not carried into the ontology.

methodological_limits: Different robot videos and differently named/task-described AI programs bundle cues. Randomized descriptions can support bounded total effects but do not isolate actual emotional capacity or one uniquely psychological mechanism.

Study 2 includes a real formal interaction and reversed simple effects. Do not replace it with a generic unequal-significance criticism. Perceived category inclusion/exclusion remains a theoretical explanation rather than a directly randomized/validated mediator.

Study 3 has a direct emotion-versus-cognition comparison, but a nonsignificant agency difference is not equivalence and significant mechanistic versus nonsignificant animalistic contrasts are not a formal test of dimension specificity.

The source regroups a three-dimension mind scale into two dimensions for theory. Alpha and agreeable directional means do not independently validate the factor structure, score coding or actual machine experience.

Post-outcome mind ratings in Study 1 and post-treatment measured mediators/controls elsewhere limit causal interpretation. Opposing mediation paths can be coherent; unknown binary coding should not be repaired by flipping signs.

A smaller human–AI gap alone does not prove human ratings fell. Separate ratings do fall modestly in Studies 4–5, which is retained, but slider anchors conflate intelligence/maturity with humanness and invite comparison/scale-use effects.

Gift-card lottery preference and a 25-cent donation have described real incentives. They are behavioral proxies, not direct workplace abuse, employee mental health or proof of a unique motive. Do not describe every choice as hypothetical or every participant as receiving$25.

Null threat, power or valence measures do not rule out every alternative, especially after outcome measurement or when included as post-treatment covariates. Brief within-session effects do not establish enduring social change.

Human dignity, rights and justified care are not conditional on a high cognitive/emotional score. Attributed capacities in a fictional AI do not establish feeling, moral personhood or a reason to treat actual people as machines.

All main pages read; full updated appendix, video content, raw data, code and registration plans remain unavailable. Source errors are documented without inferring author intent, fraud, AI generation or wholesale study invalidity.

cross_paper_learning.finding: That paper concerns capacities attributed to avatar agents; this source includes ratings of actual humans as the later target. Robot mind reduction is not automatically human dehumanization, and the exact target/measure must be preserved.
Willingness, actual choices, liking, disclosure and causal mediators differ. Here real monetary choices are retained while their relation to actual employee mistreatment remains qualified.

That source reports a null agent×behavior interaction on mind ratings. This source’s real extremity×salience interaction must be preserved rather than generalized into one universal human/robot effect.
Agency and experience can have opposing conditional coefficients, and three-dimensional scales can be regrouped. Do not repair valid suppression signs or equate high reliability with causal validity.

Score agreement and a named metric are not unique causal identification. Here smaller difference scores require separate target ratings, and those observed target changes still do not by themselves prove one mediation mechanism.

deferred.term: AI-induced or assimilation-induced dehumanization as another independent row
deferred.reason: It is a named antecedent/pathway within existing Dehumanization; preserve its evidence there and link the broader assimilation/contrast processes without synonym inflation.

deferred.term: Validated AI empathy or machine feeling
deferred.reason: Capability claims are manipulations in fictitious articles/videos, not evidence of subjective emotion or effective clinical treatment.
Measured mediators, regrouped scales, bundled task roles and missing dimension×condition tests do not isolate a universal experience-only mechanism.
The source explicitly proposes self-perception effects as future research; it does not measure them in the five main studies.

limitations: Three named judgment/categorization processes; existing IDs and eleven categories preserved. No forced citation quota, numbered rows, invented annual counts, automatic ethical/harm links, private credential use or full-paper Markdown copy.
